fullPassage:
AI is a prolific idea generator. Human brainstorming groups tend to focus on the quality of creative ideas and almost immediately lean into variations of first suggestions, but good ideas are more likely when groups focus first on quantity. As Linus Pauling put it, "The best way to have a good idea is to have lots of ideas." Psychologist Dean Keith Simonton called this the "equal odds rule" arguing that creative success is correlated to the total number of works created. Many studies have confirmed that creative quality comes from quantity of ideas (what Bob Sutton at a design and innovation consulting company called "idea ratio"), and one Stanford study pegged the number of ideas that distinguish a successful product from a failure at more than two thousand. This is why design thinking and innovation are so focused on the processes (what Utley and Klebahn call "idea flow") of ____________________.

* prolific: 많이 만들어 내는, 다작의 ** peg: 못박다

questions.passage: AI is a (A)[prolific / scarce] idea generator. Human brainstorming groups tend to focus on the quality of creative ideas and almost immediately lean into variations of first suggestions, but good ideas are more likely when groups focus first on quantity. Psychologist Dean Keith Simonton called this the "equal odds rule" arguing that creative success is (B)[correlated / unrelated] to the total number of works created. Many studies have (C)[confirmed / denied] that creative quality comes from quantity of ideas.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: AI는 다작의(prolific) 아이디어 생성자이다. 창의적 성공은 총 작품 수와 상관관계가 있다(correlated). 많은 연구가 확인했다(confirmed).
det.analysis: ✅ ① prolific-correlated-confirmed 원문 일치. ❌ ② scarce는 prolific의 반의어. ❌ ③ unrelated는 correlated의 반의어. ❌ ④ (A)(B) 맞지만 denied는 confirmed의 반의어.
det.tip: prolific ↔ scarce, correlated ↔ unrelated, confirmed ↔ denied

questions.passage: Human brainstorming groups tend to focus on the quality of creative ideas and almost (A)[immediately / gradually] lean into variations of first suggestions, but good ideas are more likely when groups focus first on quantity. Many studies have confirmed that creative quality comes from quantity of ideas, and one Stanford study pegged the number of ideas that (B)[distinguish / blur] a successful product from a failure at more than two thousand. This is why design thinking and innovation are so (C)[focused / indifferent] on the processes of generating as many ideas as possible.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 거의 즉시(immediately) 첫 제안의 변형으로 기운다. 성공적인 제품을 구별하는(distinguish) 아이디어 수. 과정에 집중한다(focused).
det.analysis: ✅ ② immediately-distinguish-focused 원문 일치. ❌ ① gradually는 immediately의 반의어. ❌ ③ (A)(C) 맞지만 blur는 distinguish의 반의어. ❌ ④ indifferent는 focused의 반의어.
det.tip: immediately ↔ gradually, distinguish ↔ blur, focused ↔ indifferent

questions.passage: Human brainstorming groups tend to focus on the quality of creative ideas and almost immediately (A)[lean into / pull back from] variations of first suggestions, but good ideas are more likely when groups focus first on quantity. Psychologist Dean Keith Simonton called this the "equal odds rule" arguing that creative (B)[success / failure] is correlated to the total number of works created. Many studies have confirmed that creative quality comes from (C)[quantity / scarcity] of ideas.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 첫 제안의 변형 쪽으로 기울다(lean into). 창의적 성공(success)은 총 작품 수와 상관. 아이디어의 양(quantity)에서 온다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③ lean into-success-quantity 원문 일치. ❌ ① pull back from은 lean into의 반의어. ❌ ② failure는 success의 반의어이지만 '창의적 실패가 상관'이면 논리 오류. ❌ ④ scarcity는 quantity의 반의어.
det.tip: lean into ↔ pull back from, success ↔ failure, quantity ↔ scarcity

questions.passage: AI is a prolific idea generator. Human brainstorming groups tend to focus on the quality of creative ideas and almost immediately lean into variations of first suggestions, but good ideas are more ①<u>likely</u> when groups focus first on quantity. Psychologist Dean Keith Simonton called this the "equal odds rule" arguing that creative success is ②<u>correlated</u> to the total number of works created. Many studies have confirmed that creative quality comes from ③<u>quantity</u> of ideas. This is why design thinking and innovation are so ④<u>detached from</u> the processes of generating as many ideas as possible.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어(구) 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 디자인 사고와 혁신이 과정에서 분리된(detached from) → 원문은 focused on(집중된). 아이디어를 많이 만드는 과정에 '집중'한다는 맥락.
det.analysis: ✅ ④ detached from(분리된)은 focused on(집중된)의 반의어. ❌ ① likely는 원문 그대로. ❌ ② correlated는 원문 그대로. ❌ ③ quantity는 원문 그대로.
det.tip: focused on(~에 집중된) ↔ detached from(~에서 분리된)

questions.passage: Human brainstorming groups tend to focus on the quality of creative ideas and almost immediately lean into ①<u>variations</u> of first suggestions, but good ideas are more likely when groups focus first on quantity. Psychologist Dean Keith Simonton called this the "equal odds rule" arguing that creative success is correlated to the ②<u>total</u> number of works created. Many studies have ③<u>confirmed</u> that creative quality comes from quantity of ideas, and one Stanford study pegged the number of ideas that ④<u>obscure</u> a successful product from a failure at more than two thousand.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 성공적인 제품을 실패와 모호하게 하는(obscure) → 원문은 distinguish(구별하는). 아이디어 수가 성공과 실패를 '구별'한다는 맥락.
det.analysis: ✅ ④ obscure(모호하게 하다)는 원문 distinguish(구별하다)의 반의어. ❌ ① variations는 원문 그대로. ❌ ② total은 원문 그대로. ❌ ③ confirmed는 원문 그대로.
det.tip: distinguish(구별하다) ↔ obscure(모호하게 하다)

questions.passage: AI is a ①<u>prolific</u> idea generator. Human brainstorming groups tend to focus on the quality of creative ideas and almost immediately ②<u>lean into</u> variations of first suggestions, but good ideas are more likely when groups focus first on quantity. Psychologist Dean Keith Simonton called this the "equal odds rule" arguing that creative success is ③<u>inversely proportional</u> to the total number of works created. Many studies have ④<u>confirmed</u> that creative quality comes from quantity of ideas.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어(구) 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 창의적 성공이 총 작품 수에 반비례한다(inversely proportional) → 원문은 correlated(상관관계가 있다). 양이 많을수록 성공한다는 논지에 반비례는 모순.
det.analysis: ✅ ③ inversely proportional(반비례)은 correlated(비례/상관)과 반대. ❌ ① lean into는 원문 그대로. ❌ ② quantity는 원문 그대로. ❌ ④ 없음 — ③이 정답.
det.tip: correlated to(~와 상관) ↔ inversely proportional to(~에 반비례)

Human brainstorming groups tend to focus on the quality of creative ideas and almost immediately lean into variations of first suggestions, but good ideas are more likely when groups focus first on ____. Psychologist Dean Keith Simonton called this the "equal odds rule" arguing that creative success is correlated to the total number of works created. Many studies have confirmed that creative quality comes from quantity of ideas (what Bob Sutton at a design and innovation consulting company called "idea ratio"), and one Stanford study pegged the number of ideas that distinguish a successful product from a failure at more than two thousand. This is why design thinking and innovation are so focused on the processes (what Utley and Klebahn call "idea flow") of ____________________.

* prolific: 많이 만들어 내는, 다작의 ** peg: 못박다
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 좋은 아이디어는 그룹이 먼저 양(quantity)에 집중할 때 더 가능성이 높다. Pauling 인용문 '많은 아이디어를 가져라'가 근거.
det.analysis: ✅ ② quantity: '많은 아이디어'라는 맥락과 일치. ❌ ① quality: 글은 quality가 아닌 quantity에 집중하라고 함. ❌ ③ diversity: 다양성이 아닌 양이 핵심. ❌ ④ originality: 독창성은 언급되지 않음.
det.tip: quantity(양) vs quality(질) — 이 글의 핵심 대비

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 성공적인 제품을 실패와 구별하는(distinguish) 아이디어의 수를 2000개 이상으로 못박았다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③ distinguish: 성공과 실패를 '구별하다'가 맥락상 정확. ❌ ① combine: 결합하다 — 성공과 실패를 결합한다는 건 부적합. ❌ ② resemble: 닮다 — 부적합. ❌ ④ merge: 합치다 — 부적합.
det.tip: distinguish A from B: A를 B와 구별하다

questions.passage: AI is a <u>prolific</u> idea generator. Human brainstorming groups tend to focus on the quality of creative ideas and almost immediately lean into variations of first suggestions.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 prolific과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: prolific = 많이 만들어 내는, 다작의 → productive(생산적인).
det.analysis: ✅ ① productive: prolific의 동의어. ❌ ② lazy: 게으른 — 반의어. ❌ ③ cautious: 신중한 — 무관. ❌ ④ limited: 제한된 — 반의어.
det.tip: prolific = productive = 많이 만들어내는

questions.passage: Psychologist Dean Keith Simonton called this the "equal odds rule" arguing that creative success is <u>correlated</u> to the total number of works created. Many studies have confirmed that creative quality comes from quantity of ideas.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 correlated와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: correlated = 상관이 있는 → associated(관련된).
det.analysis: ✅ ③ associated: correlated와 유사하게 '관련된'. ❌ ① disconnected: 분리된 — 반의어. ❌ ② identical: 동일한 — 상관은 동일이 아님. ❌ ④ opposed: 대립하는 — 반의어.
det.tip: be correlated to = be associated with = ~와 관련/상관이 있다

questions.passage: Human brainstorming groups tend to focus on the quality of creative ideas and almost immediately lean into <u>variations</u> of first suggestions, but good ideas are more likely when groups focus first on quantity.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 variations와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: variations = 변형들 → modifications(수정/변형).
det.analysis: ✅ ② modifications: variations와 동의어(변형). ❌ ① duplicates: 복제품 — 변형이 아닌 똑같은 복사. ❌ ③ originals: 원본 — 변형의 반대 개념. ❌ ④ foundations: 기초 — 무관.
det.tip: variation = modification = alteration (변형, 수정)

questions.passage: Many studies have <u>confirmed</u> that creative quality comes from quantity of ideas, and one Stanford study pegged the number of ideas that distinguish a successful product from a failure at more than two thousand.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 confirmed와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: confirmed = 확인했다 ↔ denied(부인했다).
det.analysis: ✅ ② denied: confirmed(확인)의 반의어(부인). ❌ ① verified: confirmed의 동의어. ❌ ③ validated: confirmed의 동의어. ❌ ④ supported: 지지하다 — 동의어 방향.
det.tip: confirm(확인하다) ↔ deny(부인하다)

questions.passage: Human brainstorming groups tend to focus on the quality of creative ideas and almost immediately lean into variations of first suggestions, but good ideas are more likely when groups focus first on quantity. questions.stem: 밑줄 친 focused와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: focused = 집중된 ↔ distracted(산만한).
det.analysis: ✅ ③ distracted: focused(집중된)의 반의어(산만한). ❌ ① concentrated: focused의 동의어. ❌ ② attentive: 주의 깊은 — 유의어. ❌ ④ dedicated: 헌신적인 — 유의어.
det.tip: focused(집중된) ↔ distracted(산만한)

questions.passage:
(A) Human brainstorming groups tend to focus on the quality of creative ideas and almost immediately <u>lean</u> into variations of first suggestions.

(B) The old building started to <u>lean</u> to one side after years of structural neglect.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 (A)와 (B)의 lean이 문맥에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) lean into = ~쪽으로 경도하다/기울다 (비유적). (B) lean = 기울다 (물리적).
det.analysis: ✅ ② (A) 경도하다(비유적) – (B) 기울다(물리적). ❌ ① 의미 뒤바뀜. ❌ ③ '의지하다'는 lean on. ❌ ④ '날씬한'은 형용사 lean으로 문맥 부적합.
det.tip: lean into: ~에 적극 참여하다/경도하다 vs lean: 기울다(물리적)
